concept: Volumetric DDoS exhausts a shared network link

beats.title:
Online.
But unreachable.
beats.detail: Follow the traffic to find the bottleneck.

beats.title:
One link.
Finite capacity.
beats.detail: Legitimate traffic shares a path to the service.

beats.title:
More traffic.
Same link.
beats.detail: Attack traffic converges from many devices.

beats.title: Capacity reached.
beats.detail: Packets queue. Full queues drop packets.

beats.title:
Normal traffic
gets caught too.
beats.detail: The server can remain online while access fails.

beats.title:
A full link can
block a service.
beats.detail: Shared capacity becomes an availability limit.

narration.text: The server is online. Why won't the page load?
Follow the traffic. This network link has limited capacity.
Normally, packets pass through and the service stays reachable.
Now, many devices send attack traffic toward the same destination.
Their separate paths converge on one shared link. Its capacity hasn't changed.
More traffic arrives than the link can carry. Packets wait in a queue.
When that queue fills, additional packets are dropped.
Legitimate traffic shares this bottleneck too.
A normal request may be delayed or lost before it reaches the server.
The machine can still be running while users cannot reach it.
That's one way a distributed denial of service takes a service offline.
